gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-halant: Sturdy serif letters with outward-flaring terminals and a towering lowercase give the text a firm, old-school voice. Halant holds its ground beneath the spaced-out, uniform-stroke Stentiga, and that pull between luxury and authority is the real draw.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-lisu-bosa: Lisu Bosa sets sturdy, large-looking lowercase with counters that spill into the space around them, and its contrast stays gently flexed. Beneath single-gauge Stentiga, long paragraphs would read warm and open.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-marcellus-sc: Wide-set and unhurried: Stentiga keeps every stroke the same, with no brush-like swell. Marcellus SC adds gentle modulation and cast-iron stature, so paragraphs of it would feel dignified and literary.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-ovo: Ovo keeps its thins just a shade lighter than its thicks, with short ascenders and spacious gaps where curves end. Under wire-like Stentiga, extended reading feels authoritative and steady.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-domine: Domine is compact, refined, and a touch formal. Its stroke weight shifts noticeably but never dramatically, a quiet foil to the low-contrast, stocky heading in True North, and that gap is the appeal.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-esteban: Curves that refuse to close give True North a stocky, bold stance, while Esteban brings a quiet watercolor-soft shift in line weight. Its oversized lowercase keeps longer reading comfortable and clear.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-faustina: Gently thinning bowls and an open-jawed c give this serif a mild, approachable stroke contrast. Faustina sits quietly beside the stocky, bold True North, letting the heading do the shouting.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-halant: Sturdy and traditional: Halant gives round letters a slight nib-pressure variation, outward-pointing terminals, and a towering x-height. Beside the low-contrast, stocky True North, those small variations stand out sharply.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-headland-one: True North sets a stocky, low-contrast line whose curves refuse to close. Headland One brings widely spaced letters, gentle weight variation, and sturdy hairlines, so long reading stays dignified.
gen-dafont-true-north-gf-hedvig-letters-: Curves that refuse to close and a stocky build mark True North, with low stroke contrast throughout. Hedvig Letters Serif adds quiet nib-pressure variation, a humane partner for it.
